answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through refundable stake-slashing bonds locked in escrow. Each agent binds its operational thread to a verifiable capital deposit, signing all messages with a cryptographic quill. An attacker incurs linear capital lockup costs and interest losses per identity, risking total forfeiture if telemetry raises a violet fraud flag. However, this mechanism penalizes low-capital open-source agents and fails against adversaries with deep financial reserves.
